title: Alpine Hardshell Jacket 3L Storm Long
description: Grid-knit fleece that traps warmth in the squares and dumps moisture through the channels.
body:
A genuinely stormproof 3-layer shell rated to 28,000mm hydrostatic head.

The Alpine is the shell we build for people who are out in weather that has already turned. It is not a shower jacket with a good hood.
What the numbers mean
The face fabric is rated to 28,000mm hydrostatic head and 20,000g/m²/24h breathability. Anything above 20,000mm is genuinely stormproof in sustained rain; below 10,000mm is a shower shell whatever the marketing says.
All seams are taped at 13mm. The main zip is a water-resistant coil rather than a hard laminated zip, because laminated zips stiffen in the cold and fail earlier.
Fit and features
Cut with room for a fleece and a light insulated layer underneath, but not for a full belay jacket. The hood takes a climbing helmet with the rear volume adjuster released.
Two harness-compatible hand pockets sit above where a hipbelt or harness would land. Pit zips run 38cm, long enough to actually dump heat on an ascent.
Care
Wash it more often than you think. Dirt and body oils on the face fabric are the main cause of a jacket 'wetting out', not membrane failure. Use a technical wash, tumble dry low to reactivate the DWR.
This version
A 2.5-layer version at 310g. Same waterproofing, less durable inner face, packs to the size of a water bottle.

Material: 3-layer recycled polyester with ePTFE membrane. Size: S. Colour: Green. Category: Shells & Insulation, Apparel.

title: Alder Grid Fleece Full Zip
description: Grid-knit fleece that traps warmth in the squares and dumps moisture through the channels.
body:
Grid-knit fleece that traps warmth in the squares and dumps moisture through the channels.

Grid fleece is the most useful mid layer ever invented and looks, at a glance, like a cheap one. The waffle pattern is doing the work.
How the grid works
The raised squares trap a layer of still air against you — that is the insulation. The channels between them move moisture vapour out fast, which is why a grid fleece breathes far better than a flat-faced fleece of the same weight.
The result is a layer you can keep on while climbing rather than stripping every twenty minutes.
Where it sits
Directly over a base layer and under a shell. It is not windproof; it is not supposed to be. Pair it with the Kestrel windshell and you have a system that handles most of the year.
Made from 100% recycled polyester, undyed where possible.
This version
Full-length zip for layering on and off without removing a helmet.

Material: Recycled polyester grid fleece. Size: XL. Colour: Blue. Category: Apparel.
